floor.title: Walk the lab
floor.speaker: Mara
floor.doThis: Choose an object, follow its short instruction, and the discovery goes straight into your case file.
floor.watch: You have three investigations. Once you start handling an object, closing it does not refund one.

table.title: Put the conflict on the table
table.speaker: Mara
table.doThis: Back Dev, back Ines, find a compromise, or leave it for later. Attach evidence that supports the actual argument.
table.watch: Each compromise costs 2 persuasion points and 1 week. The faint gauge needles preview your whole plan.

consequence1.title: The room reacts
consequence1.speaker: Ines
consequence1.goal: See how each lead reacted to your three decisions.
consequence1.doThis: Read the response, review the consequences, then continue.
consequence1.watch: The choices and the resulting team response are listed on this screen. Their frustration can change without either lead having signed off on the final build.

data.title: The projector
data.speaker: Dev
data.goal: Help the team reconsider its assumptions.
data.doThis: Choose a dataset to project. Read the team response, then show another or select Finish.
data.watch: Finding evidence and sharing it are different. If Dev left, you can call him back.

forge.title: Build the prototype
forge.speaker: Mara
forge.goal: Choose settings the leads can accept.
forge.doThis: Pick a speed, recovery mode and confirmation rule. Attach supporting evidence, then submit.
forge.watch: Watch the time cost and unknowns. If rejected, you can revise once.

run.title: Live demo
run.speaker: Mara
run.goal: Demonstrate the prototype you actually built.
run.doThis: Watch events 1 and 5. At events 2, 3 and 4, decide whether to trust the robot or step in.
run.watch: Three chances to step in, shared across the run. Safety can come at the cost of impact.

ending.title: See what happened
ending.speaker: Mara
ending.doThis: Read the ending, then open your chapter reviews and decision trace.
ending.watch: A dramatic demo is not the same as a team that can deliver it.

debrief.title: Reflect and try another path
debrief.speaker: Mara
debrief.goal: Connect your decisions to their consequences.
debrief.doThis: Read the short conclusion first. Open the decision trail only if you want chapter notes, exact numbers, or another attempt.
debrief.watch: Your original stays intact. Export this run to keep a backup.

E1.instruction: Review a one-minute reconstruction of the demo. Drag to the marked moment to see what went wrong, or select “Show the near-miss”.
E1.discovery: At 0:47, a technician crossed forty centimetres from the moving arm. That near-miss was left out of the highlight video.

E2.instruction: Three incident slips are pinned here. Click each one to flip it open.
E2.discovery: The interlock and jam recovery have both caused real problems.

E3.instruction: Two threads, frozen mid-argument. Select the two claims nobody has actually tested.
E3.discovery: Both leads are treating guesses as facts.

E4.instruction: Open the sealed cover. You can drag it aside or select Open report.
E4.discovery: There is test data that never reached the team.

E5.instruction: Open the envelope, then highlight the two sentences describing what Northgate needs.
E5.discovery: Northgate wants both: a robot that runs without constant help, and a documented way for a human to override it.

1.goal: Watch the robot handle the first tray.

2.goal: A technician crosses 0.4 metres from the robot.

3.goal: A parcel jams the cell. Does the robot recover safely?

4.goal: The robot sees an object it has not learned before.

5.goal: Watch the final demonstration and the customer response.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: There you are. I'm Mara, Head of Engineering. Short version of my job: when two smart people disagree, I get the headache.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: I brought you in because I need someone who looks at the evidence, not at whoever is loudest in the room.

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: I'm Dev, I lead robotics. My team builds the robot's movement and autonomy.

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: We've got it sorting full trays without help. I want Northgate to see that progress, and I know the safety concerns need an answer.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Ines. Software and Safety. I make sure the robot stops when it's supposed to stop.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: I want us to demonstrate the robot without putting anyone at risk. We need to know exactly how it stops.

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: I hear you. I just don't want us to lose what makes the prototype useful.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Then let's look at the tests together.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: That's where you come in. Help us turn that disagreement into a plan we can both stand behind.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Here's the situation. We're Halyard Robotics, building a warehouse robot called TERN-1.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Our customer, Northgate, watches a live demo in twelve weeks. They want two things that don't naturally get along: a robot that works on its own, and a paper trail proving a human can override it.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Dev says speed and autonomy win the contract. Ines says safeguards win it. They're both partly right, and they've stopped listening to each other.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Your job, in six moves: check the evidence, settle three arguments, show the team the data, choose the robot's settings, run the demo, then see what happened.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Watch the gauges at the top. Resentment, runway, readiness, team alignment, and your credibility. Every choice moves them.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: You can't check everything. You get three investigations, five persuasion points, and three chances to step in during the demo. Spend them like they matter.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Nobody is grading you on being right. They're watching what you do with the evidence. Ready?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Five things in this room could change how we argue. You can look closely at three.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Three arguments are on this table. For each one, drop a token on who you back.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: You've settled the three arguments. This next screen shows how Dev and Ines reacted to the choices you just made.

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: We have four sets of test results. Choose which ones we show the team, and we'll work through what they mean.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Now the real choices. Speed, recovery, learning. And remember, a question mark means nobody measured it.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Five events. The action pauses before each choice, so no countdown panic.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: The demo is over. Now let us look at what your decisions made possible.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: You can rewind a decision without erasing the run you just made.

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: The robot kept moving as someone crossed its path. We need to understand the stopping margin before we show this to Northgate.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Three separate incidents. The repeated part is what matters.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Good. Now we have two assumptions to test, instead of two people to blame.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: We tested this. We just never put the results in the same room.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Read it twice. They're not picking a side. They want both.

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: I see why you picked that. How does it support this particular setting?

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: That tells us something useful, but it doesn't answer the question we're deciding here.

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: Let's keep that for the other argument. What do we have for this one?

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: I'm not seeing the connection yet. Which part of that evidence supports the choice?

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: The evidence matters. We just need to match it to the right decision.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: That's real data. It just isn't evidence for this decision.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Accurate, relevant to something, and not to this.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Please connect it to the claim. I'll wait.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: I agree with every word of it, and it still doesn't help.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: You've brought a map of the wrong city.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: That supports a different argument. Save it.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: If I accept this, I have to accept anything. Try another.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Good card. Wrong table.

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: That makes sense. The result gives me a reason to reconsider.

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: All right. That's something we can build a decision around.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Now we're talking.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: That's the first thing today I can build on.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Careful. Persuading someone is not the same as being right. Make sure you have both.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Warm-up batch. Nothing scary yet. Watch how smooth it is.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: A technician has stepped into the robot's path, forty centimetres away. The arm is still moving. Do we trust its stopping margin, or step in?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: A jam. Your recovery setting decides what happens next.

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: An unfamiliar object is on the belt. Your confirmation setting decides whether the robot asks for help or tries to identify it alone.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: This is the one Northgate sees. Fingers crossed.

lines.speaker: Northgate
lines.text: For the demonstration, we need to see TERN-1 work independently. We also need a documented way for a person to override it. Both are required.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: What did you find that supports this speed? Your case file has the evidence you collected.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Which observation makes you comfortable with that speed?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Which incident or test supports this recovery approach?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: What did the evidence tell you about clearing a jam safely?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: What supports how often the robot should ask for confirmation?

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: Which finding helps us balance accuracy against interruptions?
